subject: Action requested: quick-notify path & evidence routing for potential data exposure
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@finexcorp.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: privcompliance@finexcorp.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 08:02:00 -0800
Subject: Unusual export activity — request for immediate scope & evidence

Hi Logan,

We noticed an anomalous set of object reads from one of our model endpoints that may have touched a small set of customer records. At this stage we don’t have confirmed exfiltration, but we need Redwood to treat this as a potential exposure and help us preserve evidence and confirm timelines.

Can you confirm: 
- The earliest time logs could show reads for the endpoint (granularity: minute)
- Which subprocessors could have been involved in the storage/transfer chain for inference artifacts over the last 48 hours
- Whether there is an option to get a forensic snapshot (read-only) of the relevant storage + inference telemetry

We’ve opened INC-1234 in our tracker (link below) and can provide a signed NDA/addendum if you prefer before evidence handover. This is time-sensitive — our regulator is asking for an initial notice within 24 hours pending scope.

Links: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INC-1234

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Security Ops, FinExCorp
privcompliance@finexcorp.com
[attachment: suspicious-reads.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@finexcorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unusual export activity — request for immediate scope & evidence

Alicia — thanks for the quick heads up and for opening the ticket. We’ll treat this as a potential privacy incident and follow our DPA notification playbook. Quick read on next steps from our side: 

1) Initial acknowledgement & triage (this message) — we’ll confirm what’s in scope within 4 hours.
2) Forensic snapshot request — Marcus/infra will prepare a read-only bundle. Need to confirm exact time window you want captured.
3) Subprocessor list & data flows — Kimberly will coordinate any contractual asks; Ben will map operational touchpoints.

Ben / Marcus / Kimberly — looped for action. Alicia, can you confirm the list of affected customer IDs and the 48‑hour window you referenced (start/end timestamps)? If you prefer a signed DPA addendum/NDA before we hand over the snapshot, send it over and we’ll fast-track legal review.

I’ve attached a short evidence request template that helps us collect the minimal telemetry we need (inc-evidence-request.docx).

— Logan
Logan Wright
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai
[Redwood Inference | Developer-first LLM inference]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@finexcorp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unusual export activity — request for immediate scope & evidence

Thanks. Technical notes and proposed minimal evidence package below (keeping chain-of-custody in mind):

What we can pull fast (aim: within 8 hours):
- Inference request/response logs for the endpoint (timestamped to the second)
- Worker-level kernel logs and KV-cache access logs for the relevant container IDs
- Storage access logs for any buckets/blobs referenced by the endpoint
- Snapshot of runtime metadata (model version, quantization profile, batch sizes)

Potential subprocessors in the data path (to our knowledge):
- CloudStorageCo (object storage for customer payloads) — may have processed exports if the service was configured to offload snapshots
- EdgeServe Ltd. (optional edge caching layer for low-latency customers)
- CDNPartner X (delivery of large telemetry bundles; only used for large exports)

Chain-of-custody controls we’ll apply: read-only snapshot, SHA256 manifests for each archive, limited S3 presigned URL with 72h expiry, and an internal audit record of who accessed the bundle.

Attachments we’ll prepare: forensic_snapshot_v1.tar (read-only bundle), redwood-soc2-2025.pdf (requested proof of controls). If FinExCorp needs direct transfer to an on-prem escrow, confirm the SFTP endpoint and PGP key.

Kimberly — please confirm whether we should treat this as an event that triggers the DPA 72h notification obligation or as a lower-severity alert. FinEx’s ask to get an initial notice within 24h is noted; we need a quick determination of data types affected (PII/PHI/financial identifiers) to finalize legal position.

Quoted for context: 
> From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@finexcorp.com>
> We noticed an anomalous set of object reads from one of our model endpoints that may have touched a small set of customer records.

— Ben Carter
Security Incident Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
[attachment: none]

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@finexcorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 12:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unusual export activity — request for immediate scope & evidence

Thanks Ben & team — this is helpful. FinEx confirms: 
- Affected customer IDs: FEX-2001, FEX-2032, FEX-2109 (we’ll upload a vetted list to the Jira ticket).
- Window: 2026-11-13T22:00:00Z through 2026-11-14T06:00:00Z (UTC) — please capture that range.
- Data types: account identifiers, masked card fingerprints, and a small set of names/email addresses. No unmasked SSNs or raw PAN data expected.

We accept the read-only snapshot approach and request: 
- Evidence transferred via presigned URL to our SECURE bucket (we’ll provide ARN and IAM role if required)
- Redaction assistance on any logs that reference non-FinEx customer IDs
- Confirmation whether any cross-border transfers will be performed during collection/analysis (we prefer evidence to remain in-us regionally)

We will send a signed DPA addendum via DocuSign; I’ll include a contact for our compliance counsel. Please proceed with the forensic snapshot prep and share the SHA256 manifest when ready.

Appreciate the rapid response — regulator timeline noted.

Alicia
Head of Security Ops, FinExCorp
[attachment: vetted_customer_list.csv (CSV, 3KB)]
